key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum computers can simulate atomic nuclei using nuclear shell-model and no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians, extending quantum advantage efforts beyond chemistry.
engineering_relevance: It provides the first resource estimates for nuclear quantum simulation, helping engineers assess whether near-term fault-tolerant hardware can support realistic nuclear-physics workloads.
method: Constructed and compiled quantum algorithms for effective shell-model Hamiltonians.
Extended the approach to no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians with three-body interactions from chiral effective field theory.
Estimated Toffoli gate counts and qubit requirements for representative nuclei.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports resource estimates for nuclei such as 32Mg and 219At, and compares them against recent Femoco chemistry benchmarks, while finding much higher costs for no-core-shell-model cases up to about 40Ca.
watch_item: No-core-shell-model simulations appear substantially more expensive, so practical implementations will likely require more specialized algorithms and hardware-efficient strategies.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for simulating atomic nuclei
